IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r1.claim: The source identifies the الإنسان in 80:24 as ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r1.anchor: والسابع عشر : عتبة بن أبي لهب . [ ومنه ] قوله تعالى في عبس : ﴿ فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه ﴾

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p186/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p186/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p186/r3.claim: If earlier proofs fail to persuade, reflection on food and the rain that sustains it shows resurrection is easy for God and that providential favor entails accountability.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p186/r3.anchor: Man should only reflect on the food on which his life depends

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p187/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p187/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p187/r1.claim: Sincere reflection on abundant, varied food and rain shows that resurrection is easy for God and that people will answer for their duties toward divine favors.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p187/r1.anchor: The very rain which is a means of his subsistence practically demonstrates this fact

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r12.claim: After listing favors in human creation, God turns people to food and the processes that make it edible; most take food literally, while others say reflect on its excrement and worldly transience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r12.anchor: ولما عدد تعالى نعمه في نفس الإنسان، ذكر النعم فيما به قوام حياته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

JISHUMI:v10p7291/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r1.claim: The water poured down is rain from clouds, though the wording can encompass other waters because God brings them forth.
JISHUMI:v10p7291/r1.anchor: أي: أنزلنا الغيث من السحاب إنزالا، يحتمل أنه يريد المطر، ويحتمل سائر المياه

ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r13.claim: People should examine their food and its gradual growth to recognize inner and outer blessings, give thanks, and use them rightly.
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r13.anchor: nasıl bir kudret ve hikmet ile peyderpey terakki ederek yetiştirildiğine nazar etsin

ZAJJAJ:v5p285/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p285/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p285/r3.claim: People should consider how God created their food and the food of all animals as a means of their lives.
ZAJJAJ:v5p285/r3.anchor: أي فلينظر الإنسان كيف خلق الله طعامه وطعام جميع الحيوان الذي جعله الله سببا لحياتهم.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p492/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p492/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p492/r2.claim: In Abasa human food is listed first, so people precede livestock in the closing phrase; the sequence first names grains and fruit for people, then fodder for animals.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p492/r2.anchor: ذكر طعام الإنسان من الحب والفواكه أولاً ثم ذكر طعام الأنعام بعده

ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r1.claim: Since people have not fulfilled what they were commanded despite the prior blessings that call for obedience, they should consider their food, perhaps this prompts fulfillment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r1.anchor: على معنى إذا كان هذا حال الإنسان وهو أنه إلى الآن لم يقض ما أمره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r2.speaker: العصامية
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r2.claim: Al-Isami's marginal note says the rebuke that people have not fulfilled their command strongly stirs them to obey the following command to look; the transition assumes obedience follows abandoning their present course.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r2.anchor: وفي الحواشي العصامية لا يخفى ما في قوله تعالى لما يقض ما أمره من كمال تهييج الإنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r3.claim: The apparent referent is humankind generally, as in the earlier statement 'man is destroyed'; al-Isami allows a universal failure to fulfill, with the commanded observer distinct from the disbelieving human meant by the failure.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالإنسان هنا نحو ما أريد به في قوله تعالى قتل الإنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r4.claim: The discussion contrasts blessings inherent to the human self and its needs with external blessings; proposed alternatives call the first special and second general, or the first about coming into being and second about continued life, the latter distinction being questionable.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r4.anchor: نعم الذاتية أي ما يتعلق بذات الإنسان من الذات نفسها ولوازمها وهذا ذكر النعم الخارجية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r5.claim: Food means consumables of every kind; drink is omitted because food displays more signs of divine power, while explaining the omission by subsuming drink is unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p45#3/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالطعام المطعوم بأنواعه واقتصر عليه ولم يذكر المشروب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p338#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p338#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p338#2/r4.claim: After mentioning human creation, God mentions sustenance so people will reflect on how He measured and arranged food as a cause of life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p338#2/r4.anchor: كيف قدره ربه ودبره له وجعله سببا لحياته.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p338#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p338#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p338#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid interprets looking at one's food as looking at one's entry and exit.

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:21-25/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:21-25/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:21-25/r5.claim: The passage moves from blessings intrinsic to the person to external blessings.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p329/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p329/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p329/r6.claim: People should examine their food with sight and insight, considering God’s craft and their dependence: without His provision they would perish.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p329/r6.anchor: يوقع النظر التام على كل شيء يقدر على النظر به من بصره وبصيرته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p329/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p329/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p329/r7.claim: The food passage begins with the sky and water because they are exalted and water sustains life; it recalls the human’s first creation and dependence on the whole world.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p329/r7.anchor: وبدأ أولا بالسماوي لأنه أشرف , وبالماء الذي هو حياة كل شيء , تنبيها له على ابتداء خلقه

DURR-FULL:v8p419/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb quotes a divine admonition said to be in the Torah or the scripture of Abraham: God recounts creating and nurturing the human, then calls the disobedient person to invoke Him as near, responsive, forgiving, and merciful.
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال: قرأت في التوراة أو قال في مصحف إبراهيم فوجدت فيها

DURR-FULL:v8p419/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr takes looking at one’s food as considering where it enters and where it exits.
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير في قوله: {فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه} قال: إلى مدخله ومخرجه

DURR-FULL:v8p419/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r4.claim: Mujahid gives the same explanation: consider the food’s entrance and exit.

DURR-FULL:v8p419/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the food here as human excrement.
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه} قال: إلى خرئه

DURR-FULL:v8p419/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says an angel bends Adam’s neck when he sits to relieve himself so he can see what comes out.
DURR-FULL:v8p419/r6.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: {فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه} قال: ملك يثني رقبة ابن آدم إذا جلس على الخلاء

DURR-FULL:v8p420/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p420/r1.speaker: أبو قلابة
DURR-FULL:v8p420/r1.claim: Abu Qilaba quotes a Torah admonition to look at what one hoarded and what it became, pointing to the transformation of food into waste.
DURR-FULL:v8p420/r1.anchor: عن أبي قلابة قال: مكتوب في التوراة يا ابن آدم انظر إلى ما بخلت به إلى ما صار

DURR-FULL:v8p420/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p420/r2.speaker: بشير بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p420/r2.claim: Bashir ibn Kaʿb would take his companions to a refuse heap and ask them to see what became of the honey, ghee, and food once in people’s bellies.
DURR-FULL:v8p420/r2.anchor: عن بشير بن كعب أنه كان يقول لأصحابه إذا فرغ من حديثه: انطلقوا حتى أريكم الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3401/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3401/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3401/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says an angel turns the son of Adam's neck when he sits in the latrine so he looks at what comes out.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3401/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : فلينظر الانسان إلى طعامه قال : ملك يثني رقبة ابن ادم اذا جلس علي الخلاء لينظر ما يخرج منه .

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33/r1.claim: After mentioning human creation, the passage turns to provision so people reflect and infer resurrection from the growth of plants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر خلق ابن آدم ذكر رزقه ليعتبر وليستدل بالنبات على البعث

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33/r2.claim: Muqatil identifies the person here as Utba ibn Abi Lahab.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل يعني به عتبة بن أبي لهب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33/r3.claim: The command means to look at how God created the food He made a cause of human life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p33/r3.anchor: ومعنى الكلام فلينظر الإنسان كيف خلق الله طعامه الذي جعله سببا لحياته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p323/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p323/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p323/r5.claim: Food is a blessing and evidence: God revives plants from dead earth as He will revive bodies from decayed bones and scattered dust.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p323/r5.anchor: (فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه) فيه امتنان، وفيه استدلال بإحياء النبات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r1.claim: After enumerating blessings in the human being, the passage turns to blessings needed for life and calls people to consider how God arranged their food.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r1.anchor: ولما عدد النعم في نفسه : أتبعه ذكر النعم فيما يحتاج إليه ، فقال : { فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r2.claim: Food means the sustenance by which people live; ‘We poured water’ refers to rain.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r2.anchor: إلى مطعمه الذي يعيش به كيف دبرنا أمره ( أنا صببنا الماء ) يعني الغيث .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r14.claim: The passage thanks God for provisions; context makes clear that al-abb is a plant God provides for people or livestock, so general understanding suffices until its exact botanical referent becomes clear.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p704/r14.anchor: فأراد أن الآية مسوقة في الامتنان علي الإنسان بمطعمه واستدعاء شكره ، وقد علم من فحوى الآية أن الأب بعض ما أنبته الله للإنسان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r1.claim: After enumerating blessings in the human being, the passage turns to blessings needed for life and calls people to consider how God arranged their food.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r1.anchor: ولما عدد النعم في نفسه : أتبعه ذكر النعم فيما يحتاج إليه ، فقال : { فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r2.claim: Food means the sustenance by which people live; ‘We poured water’ refers to rain.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r2.anchor: إلى مطعمه الذي يعيش به كيف دبرنا أمره ( أنا صببنا الماء ) يعني الغيث .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r14.claim: The passage thanks God for provisions; context makes clear that al-abb is a plant God provides for people or livestock, so general understanding suffices until its exact botanical referent becomes clear.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p705/r14.anchor: فأراد أن الآية مسوقة في الامتنان علي الإنسان بمطعمه واستدعاء شكره ، وقد علم من فحوى الآية أن الأب بعض ما أنبته الله للإنسان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r4.speaker: يحيى
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r4.claim: Yahya says people should consider the food they eat and live by, whatever it may be.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r4.anchor: إلى طعامه الذي يأكله وتحيا نفسه به , من أي شيء كان , قاله يحيى

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r5.claim: Another interpretation is that people should consider whatever comes out of them and what becomes of it after preserving life while the body dies.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r5.anchor: ما يخرج منه أي شيء كان ؟ ثم كيف صار بعد حفظ الحياة وموت الجسد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r6.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says an angel bends Adam's neck when he sits to relieve himself so he can see what comes out.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r6.anchor: قال الحسن : إن ملكا يثني رقبة ابن آدم إذا جلس على الخلاء لينظر ما يخرج منه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r7.claim: Considering bodily waste may remind people that it is a locus of filth and keep them from arrogance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r7.anchor: ليعلم أنه محل الأقذار فلا يطغى

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r8.claim: Considering bodily waste may also prompt reflection on the transformation of bodies and prevent forgetfulness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p206/r8.anchor: ليستدل على استحالة الأجسام فلا ينسى

MUQATIL:80:24-32/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:24-32/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:24-32/r1.claim: The person told to consider is Utba ibn Abi Lahab.
MUQATIL:80:24-32/r1.anchor: يعني عتبة بن أبى لهب { إلى طعامه }

MUQATIL:80:24-32/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:24-32/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:80:24-32/r12.claim: The Prophet said that people were created from seven, provided for from seven, and brought forth upon seven.
MUQATIL:80:24-32/r12.anchor: خلقتم من سبع، ورزقتم من سبع، وخرجتم على سبع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p318#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p318#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p318#4/r1.claim: A person should consider the food he eats and lives by, and how God arranged its provision.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p318#4/r1.anchor: الذى يأكله ويحيا به كيف دبرنا أمره

BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r3.claim: The passage begins counting the blessings that preserve life, following the earlier account of blessings involved in human origination.

BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r4.claim: People should consider their food and how God has arranged their sustenance.
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r4.anchor: أي فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه الذي عليه يدور أمر معاشه كيف دبرناه

BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says looking at one’s food teaches the lowliness of one’s status and the shortness of one’s life.
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r5.anchor: فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه ليعلم خسة قدره وفناء عمره

BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r6.claim: A hadith makes Adam’s food an example of the world: even after seasoning and salting it, one should see what it ultimately becomes.
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r6.anchor: إن مطعم ابن آدم جعله الله مثلا للدنيا وإن قزحه وملحه فنظر إلى ماذا يصير

BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r7.claim: Qazzaḥa means adding spices to a pot; qizāḥ is seasoning, and malaḥa means adding salt.
BURSEVI:v10p262#2/r7.anchor: يقال قزح القدر جعل التابل فيها وهو كصاحب وهاجر إبزار الطعام وملحها جعل الملح فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r1.claim: After mentioning human creation, God directs people to consider how He created food and arranged life's necessities, so they may prepare for the afterlife.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r1.anchor: لما ذكر جل ثناؤه ابتداء خلق الإنسان، ذكر ما يسر من رزقه أي فلينظر كيف خلق الله طعامه

QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r2.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid interpret ‘his food’ as what enters and exits the body.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r2.anchor: وروي عن الحسن ومجاهد قالا: { فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه } أي إلى مدخله ومخرجه.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r3.claim: The Prophet asked al-Dahhak ibn Sufyan al-Kilabi what he ate; after meat and milk, he asked what it became, then said what leaves Adam's body is a parable of worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك بن سفيان الكلابي قال: قال لي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يا ضحاك ما طعامك» قلت: يا رسول الله! اللحم واللبن

QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r4.claim: The Prophet says Adam's food is a parable of the world, however well seasoned, and one should consider what it becomes.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r4.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r5.claim: Abu al-Walid asked Ibn ʿUmar about looking at excrement in the privy; an angel asks what the thing hoarded has become.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:24-25/r5.anchor: وقال أبو الوليد: سألت ابن عمر عن الرجل يدخل الخلاء فينظر ما يخرج منه قال: يأتيه الملك فيقول انظر ما بخلت به إلى ما صار؟

STUDYQURAN:80:24/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:24/r1.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:80:24/r1.claim: One view takes food as a sign for reflection that helps people appreciate God's power and mercy.
STUDYQURAN:80:24/r1.anchor: signs upon which human beings should reflect in order to appreciate fully God’s Power and Mercy (Q)

STUDYQURAN:80:24/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:24/r2.speaker: Others
STUDYQURAN:80:24/r2.claim: Another view links reflection on eating and elimination to what becomes of the world.
STUDYQURAN:80:24/r2.anchor: Others say that it relates to reflecting upon the consumption and elimination of food, for that is an example of what becomes of the world (Q).

TABATABAI:80:24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:24/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:24/r2.claim: The human in 80:24 is everyone, unlike the extreme disbeliever in 80:17; the author notes that the noun is repeated explicitly rather than replaced by a pronoun.
TABATABAI:80:24/r2.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان - كما قيل - غير الإنسان المتقدم المذكور

TABATABAI:80:24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:24/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:24/r3.claim: The command follows the previous general point by directing everyone to consider the food that sustains life, one of innumerable provisions prepared by divine governance to meet human needs.
TABATABAI:80:24/r3.anchor: توجيه نظر الإنسان إلى طعامه الذي يقتات به ويستمد منه لبقائه وهو واحد مما لا يحصى

TABATABAI:80:24/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:24/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:24/r4.claim: Reflection on food reveals the vast, astonishing scope of divine planning and God's precise, comprehensive care for human welfare and the order of life.
TABATABAI:80:24/r4.anchor: سعة التدبير الربوبي التي تدهش لبه وتحير عقله، وتعلق العناية الإلهية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p227/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p227/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p227/r1.claim: People should consider how God created their food and made it a cause of life; the focus is its coming into existence, which invites reflection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p227/r1.anchor: أي فلينظر كيف خلق الله طعامه الذي جعله سببا لحياته

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:20-28/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:20-28/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:20-28/r6.claim: People should consider how their Lord measured and arranged their food.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:20-28/r6.anchor: فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه } كيف قدره ربه ودبره له.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r1.claim: After summarizing divine favors concerning human existence and nature in verses 18–20, the passage recalls external blessings that sustain human life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r1.anchor: Yukarıda 18-20. âyetlerde insanın var oluşu ve mahiyetine ilişkin ilâhî lütuflar özetlenmişti; burada ise onu çevreleyen ve varlığını sürdürmesi için gerekli ve faydalı olan haricî nimetlerin başlıcaları hatırlatılmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r2.claim: The reminders aim to inform people of God's great power and strengthen faith, and to move them to grateful worship and obedience in response to His favors.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:24/r2.anchor: Bu hatırlatmanın amacı da hem muhatabı Allah’ın kudretinin büyüklüğü hakkında bilgilendirip iman etmesini veya inancını güçlendirmesini sağlamak hem de onu bu lütuflarından dolayı Allah’a minnet ve şükran hisleriyle ibadet etmeye, buyruklarına göre yaşamaya yöneltmektir.

THALABI:v10p133/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p133/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p133/r1.claim: The Prophet asks al-Dahhak ibn Sufyan what he eats and what it becomes, then says what leaves Adam’s body is an example of worldly life.
THALABI:v10p133/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك بن سفيان الكلابي: إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له: «يا ضحاك ما طعامك؟»

THALABI:v10p133/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p133/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p133/r2.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reports the Prophet saying human food represents the world; even when seasoned, one should consider what it becomes.
THALABI:v10p133/r2.anchor: عن الحسن عن عتي عن أبي بن كعب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن مطعم ابن آدم جعل مثلا للدنيا

THALABI:v10p133/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p133/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v10p133/r3.claim: Ibn Umar says an angel tells someone inspecting his excrement to see what he had been miserly with and what it became.
THALABI:v10p133/r3.anchor: سألت ابن عمر عن الرجل يدخل الخلاء فينظر إلى ما يخرج منه، قال: يأتيه الملك

DAMGHANI:v1p51/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r3.claim: In the rebuke “Perish man,” al-insān means ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab; the same referent appears in the command to look at food.
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r3.anchor: الرابع عشر : الإنسان عتبة بن أبي لهب . قوله تعالى في سورة عبس

NAHHAS:v5p151/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p151/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p151/r11.claim: The sentence ends at verse 24 for Medinan readers and Abu Amr, but not for Kufans, who connect it causally to the next verse.
NAHHAS:v5p151/r11.anchor: تمام على قراءة المدنيين وأبي عمرو وعلى قراءة الكوفيين ليس بتمام
